record.question: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
options: The Chief Justice of Supreme Court
record.explanation: Answer A: The President. Article 324(2) of the Constitution provides that the President appoints the Chief Election Commissioner, subject to any law Parliament makes on the matter. This authority also applied in March 2010. Historical/source note: Distinguish formal appointment authority from the procedure for recommending/selecting a candidate. Reference: https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/08/7af1daa22d65f9d04c00ae9b9aa5a799.pdf. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Historical facts are anchored to the original exam; no matching examiner key is asserted.
